correctness.rationale: For every generic central normal the minimum of the three squared plane-direction coordinates selects the active cylinder. Pairwise ties on six signed great-circle lines are active exactly when |n_k|<|n_i+s n_j|. Sorting absolute normal components exhaustively yields three active antipodal lines in the triangle chamber and four in the dominant chamber. The polar area integral on each arc is exactly the transformed-polar-angle increment divided by |n_i|, producing the finite atan2 sum. The 24 disjoint spherical right-cone chambers have individual solid angle 2 arctan(3-2 sqrt(2)); this proves the probability. The embedded verifier independently compares area against direct 25000-point midpoint integration and counts against inequalities; finite tests are not universal proofs.

value.rationale: The tricylinder is a natural intersection solid with well-known bulk intrinsic volumes but more complicated orientation-resolved sections. The final theorem completely classifies its generic conic-arc topology, constructs exact junction directions and converts every central-plane area to a reproducible finite elementary expression. These data are geometrically motivated and enable exact per-direction slicing or further distribution/extremal studies. The known numerical cube probability is acknowledged as prior art; value rests on the new geometry and area formula.
